Question: Some people believe that studying at university or college is the best route to a successful career, while others believe that it is better to get a job straight after school. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

Essay:
People these days have different views about what students should do after they leave school. While many people claim that school leavers should secure a job, I would claim that it is better for them to pursue universities or colleges.

On the one hand, for those who want to get a job straight after high school, they believe that this is beneficial for some reasons. Firstly, since they take part in workforce early, they can make money and save a large amount of money which enable them to afford their interest in travelling or shopping. In fact, they can get payment each month and do not have to waste money on tuition fee or school materials. Secondly, this can be seen as an opportunity for the young to accumulate practical experience and useful skills. This can be explained by the face that curriculums in accademic institution include many subjects which might not concentrate on the skills meeting the demand of the jobs. Therefore, getting involve in the real workforce can be a good ways to develop these skills. 

On the other hand, I believe that the school leavers should attend higher school as it is the best way to success in their future career. First of all, most of the top careers which receive admiration from the public require accademic qualifications as an essential condition to be hired. For example, to become a doctor of a layer, individuals are forced to study 4-6 years in universities otherwise their appication would be not meet the requirement of the occupation. In addition, those who graduate from accademic institution have a better chance to get high salary jobs.  That is because they are classified in qualified employees who is taught to think and solve problem logically. Certaintly, the employers have more interest in people with university's degree than school leavers and are more likely to be willing to pay more for them. 

In conclusion, while many people believe peole should get a job straight after school, I would argue that university can give them a better future in their career.

Question: People nowadays tend to have children at older ages. 

Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.

Essay:
Most people’s dream is to have children of their own. In recent times, some individuals decide to give birth at a later age. Although there are some benefits attached to that, such as mental and emotional maturity, as well as financial stability, however, there are also risks of having a baby with deformity, not being able to give children optimum parenting due to unavailability, which I believe outweigh the benefits. 

To begin, so many people in this modern society would rather prefer to pursue their career first, get a job and have a steady income before venturing into marriage and childbearing. Their reason is that it makes it very easy to train the children without having to face the challenges of finance, as such children mostly lack nothing. For instance, when one is financially buoyant, they can afford to train their children to any level of education. More so, some people also think that it’s better to be mentally mature enough to be able to face the emotional ups and downs that come with childbearing and parenting. 

On the other hand, as some people are busy pursuing their careers, they tend to forget that age is not on their side, hence old age increases one’s chances of giving birth to abnormal babies. Furthermore, when parents are busy  and so engulfed with their job, they have little or no time to monitor their youngsters and attend to their needs. In addition, early retirement age might catch up with one, thereby affecting their income, and besides, old age comes with weakness and poses the risk of lack of energy required to control children. For instance, an elderly man who has  a two-year-old toddler would find it tasking to walk the baby around the house.

In conclusion, in as much as there are advantages to early childbearing and upbringing such as a steady income, and mental and emotional maturity, the disadvantages which include, lack of availability due to busy schedules, and having babies with congenital anomalies exceed the advantages.

Question: Some people believe that studying at university or college is the best route to a successful career, while others believe that it is better to get a job straight after school.

Question: Some people think that one of the best ways to solve environmental problems is to increase the cost of fuel. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
The world is now surrounded by many urgent environmental problems, and many people feel that raising the cost of fuel is one of the most effective ways of combatting them. Although I tend to agree with this viewpoint, I believe there are other environmental measures that need to be taken. 

Increasing petrol prices would help save the environment in many ways. As the number of vehicles on the roads is increasing dramatically, so is the amount of vehicular emissions released into the atmosphere. However, if governments increase fuel costs, this solution would serve as a deterrent for people who drive their private cars, reducing air pollution and ozone layer depletion. Besides discouraging people from driving their private cars, this would also generate income to make further investments in environmental initiatives. Given these potential benefits of raising fuel prices, is it hardly surprising to see so many countries applying it to practice.

Apart from increasing the cost of fuel, we can also implement other solutions to environmental issues. For instance, on an individual level, people who want to help the environment should become more environmentally responsible by buying eco-friendly products, and reusing and recycling plastic bags. They can also take public transport as opposed to their personal cars, which produce toxic fumes. From a government’s perspective, it is essential to switch to green energy sources, such as solar and wind, rather than continuing to rely on gas and petrol. Thus, environmental protection goes beyond just raising fuel prices. 

In conclusion, though I attach great importance to the practice of increasing fuel costs, I think that both individuals and governing bodies should become environment-oriented in their mindset to tackle environmental problems.

This acts as an incentive for the overexploitation of national elements, shaking the environmental equilibrium and decelerating the rehabilitation.

Question: Some people think the main purpose of school is to turn children into good citizens and workers, rather than to benefit them as individuals.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
Many are of the opinion that the primary role of schools is to create good citizens, instead of simply working towards individual betterment. In my opinion, schools should aim to elevate the individual, not impose conformity.

Those in favour of this statement argue the value of a well-functioning society. As the world develops and there are advances in medicine, safety, working conditions, and so on it is easy to forget that this level of comfort requires sacrifices for the common good. Individuals must work at companies to stimulate the economy and the public must have a basic sense of community in order to live peaceably with one’s neighbours. School is where this education can begin. Teachers can explicitly and implicitly guide students to socially beneficial behaviours and educate them well enough to establish a viable future career.

However, I would argue that focusing on the individual will accomplish the goals detailed above but also be mentally healthier. Students who are taught to share, work well in teams, and develop their talents will contribute to society as a byproduct of pursuing their own seemingly selfish interests. Moreover, there may be times when the focus on society will come at the cost of the mental health of individuals. For instance, students who are taught to withhold their personal viewpoints in school, as is common in many authoritarian nations, may harbour resentment and not feel they can fully express themselves in a free environment. Psychological research has shown that the key to healthy growth is feeling safe to express oneself without fear of reprisals and repercussions.

In conclusion, although there is a valid argument in favour of social stability, schools should aim to produce healthy, industrious individuals. Naturally, these goals are not mutually exclusive and the overlap should be emphasized.

Question: Some people think that art is an essential subject for children at school while others think it is a waste of time. Discuss both views and give your opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Painting or music is a compulsory subject in most of the schools nowadays. While some think that there are much more important subjects, others believe that art is a very crucial field to learn. To begin with, subjects like science or technology may sometimes outweigh the significance of drawing or craftwork for various reasons. Firstly, in the practical world, people are only looking for an education which could provide them with a better or secured job. For example, studying mathematics may ensure a better future than painting. Secondly, nowadays kids are very much pressurized by so many different tasks or extracurricular activities, thus parents may want to teach only what could be fruitful in the near future for the children. For instance, a kid takes lessons on mathematics, science, karate and swimming, as a result, any less important area may make an extra burden on the tiny shoulder. On the contrary, music or sculpture may help to grow a child's fundamental knowledge or heal mental stress. There are ample of important subjects a child could learn, however art is definitely one of them. It helps to express inner feelings, explore new things and nourishes minds. For example, an artistic mind is always innovative, hence a kid could experience many things by this. Also, if the student is interested in this, he could choose it as a profession. In other words, Leonardo Da Vinci was a great artist and there is no doubt about his extremely successful career. Moreover, there are so many positive aspects of learning art in school that it could never be a spared.

In conclusion, this essay has discussed both views. Although both views have merits and demerits, I reckon that it is very much needed to include artwork as a compulsory subject in primary education in order to build the students' basic understanding in this matter.

Question: Today, people are surrounded by advertising. This affects what people think is important and has a negative impact on people's lives. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
In the contemporary era, the existence of advertising has crept into many aspects of daily life. From my perspective, this tendency has raised many disruptive concerns relating to the issues of manipulating public opinion and fostering overshopping.

To begin with, the popularity of advertisements can form a negative perspective on daily activities. It is true that the high density of advertisements leads to memorable footage stuck in the audience's minds. This might have the impact of changing their mindset in the long-term whether they are exposed to too many of these advertisements. For example, people watching car advertisements usually recognize that the background of these tends to be decorated in a luxurious way leading to a mindset that only the high-order classes can buy them. Because the target audiences of car sellers are often the high-income people, however, it could be seen that advertisements release in the public eye. Thus, it is understandable that many people hold a belief that owning a car is a represented aspect belonging to the rich community. Nevertheless, it is noticeable that this is a mistrustful idea and stereotype, and many forms of advertisements are manipulating the public to push their sales.

Furthermore, the high density has not only shifted people’s perspective  but also led to detrimental activities. Firstly, many advertisements promoting their items tend to constantly repeat not only on TV and smartphones  but also on billboards whether people going out, this would stick in customers’ memories and lead to a feeling of curiosity or fear of missing out. Therefore, trending products are usually hunted and attracted by a plethora of consumers. However, there are a variety of top trending products from several aspects of the market, leading to the customers’ tendency to splash all their money on them. It reckons that this is an expenditure habit and also harms the surrounding environment due to the high demands of producing too many items. Zara, a fashion brand, for example, is a well-known case of fast fashion. This company is usually boycotted because it would like to release a new collection for every new season and overproduct them. Therefore, the consumption is always lower than the production and the leftovers actually contribute to the global garbage dump more seriously.

In conclusion, it is true that many advertisements around daily lives have many highlighted negative impacts, including distorting the audiences’ views or breeding overconsumption.

Question: Consumers are faced with increasing numbers of advertisements from competing companies. To what extent do you think are consumers influenced by advertisements? What measures can be taken to protect them?

Essay:
It has been reported that consumers today encounter more advertisements than they used to. In my opinion, this phenomenon has brought about tremendous disadvantages to customers as it prompts them to spend more money. The customers, therefore, should be protected by practising self-control.

In the past, people were faced with advertisements on a few occasions. Back then, mainstream media, such as television and newspapers, were some of the only ways for companies to introduce their products and persuade customers to buy them. As a result, if people had seen a wanted item through a television or newspaper advert, they would have had a long time before they could see it again and thus may reconsider whether the product was necessary. However, advertisements have changed significantly in the last few decades and have appeared in every social media platform people access. As customers constantly use those media websites, they have to face the product adverts many times and eventually succumb to the urge to buy them. For example, Vietnamese youngsters have spent more money on unnecessary, low-quality items because of pop-up advertisements on their Facebook pages.

As most of those advertisements usually do not violate any national law, I believe governments cannot interfere with the way companies sell their goods. Therefore, customers may have to learn self-control and budget management themselves to avoid the adverse impact of increasing adverts. For instance, they could reduce their hours online to prevent advertisement encounters. If they cannot use social media less, they must shut down adverts as soon as they see them. Additionally, financial considerations should be taken to decide if a product is worth buying before its purchase.

In conclusion, facing rising advertisements leads to more expenses among people. I believe that in this case, self-discipline and deep consideration should be practised to mitigate unnecessary expenditure.

Question: Housing shortage in big cities can cause severe social consequences. Some people think only government action can solve this problem. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
The scarcity of land to build new houses is a problem that many countries are facing around the world. This issue is more evident in big cities and results in serious results such as high cost of living and poor quality of life. Therefore, many experts recommend that only the government can take the required measurements to handle it efficiently. Personally, I strongly agree with the given statement as it is only the regime can plan a city in a better way and provide better opportunities to its residents. 

The foremost reason for supporting the above statement is that it is only the state that has the authority to plan and organise cities as well as their infrastructure. Thus, in order to save space, it should discourage building single-storey residences by constructing multi-storey buildings equipped with all facilities and providing them to the public at reasonable prices. For example, to solve the issue of unavailability of homes, the Singapore government built vertical complexes with the collaboration of the housing department which were not only cheaper but also well organised. Besides, the state can implement laws in this regard. To illustrate the Canadian government, in view of the increasing prices of apartments, brought the law to restrict purchasing them by foreigners.

Additionally, to discourage people from migrating to urban cities, better amenities can be made available in the countryside only since many folks move to urban areas in search of opportunities related to education, medical and employment. For instance, when the authority levied less tax on companies which would establish their offices and factories in rural areas, fewer people migrated to city centres. As a result, it solved the issue of congested spaces, especially in the centre of the city.

In conclusion, it is evident that it is only the state which can take proper steps in order to solve the problem related to the shortage of housing in urban spaces by investing more in the countryside and encouraging people to live in vertical buildings instead of landed houses. I also highly suggest taking mentioned steps to solve the above problem.

Question: Some people think that robots are important for human’s future development. Others think that robots have negative effects on society. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

Essay:
Nowadays we are surrounded more than ever with technology, and robots are becoming more and more common in various types of scenarios. Of course, there are just about as many pros as cons to their presence in human lives, but overall I consider their role in human development to be very valuable. 

On the one hand, I do agree with the fact that these androids have been considered to contribute enormously to human development. They are great at performing repetitive functions, such as those involved in the production of different goods. They are also amazing at carrying out very detailed actions and can be seen now participating in a few select surgeries.  Not only do they excel in many different responsibilities such as health care and production, but they also allow humans to focus on more complex and sensitive projects. For example, they are very good at practical work but aren't as effective when it comes to taking care of the elderly. This type of task requires a more empathetic and emotional approach, which remains a more distinctively human capability.

Despite all the amazing work robots do, there are quite a few negative effects on society that must contemplated. To begin with, since these machines can execute simple duties originally performed by humans, they are gradually taking over people's positions, affecting the labour market drastically. For instance, it is becoming more and more common to see cashier-free checkout points in supermarkets all over the world. There is also a concern about safety-related efforts performed by bots. For example, in the industry of autonomous vehicles robots are given partial control of a vehicle that transports humans and must overcome a series of different obstacles to get to their destination. In my opinion, there is no doubt that they have still a lot to learn to be able to perform such complex human actions. 

In conclusion, while robots undoubtedly contribute significantly to human development, we must carefully navigate the potential drawbacks they pose. Striking a balance between embracing their positive impacts and mitigating negative consequences, such as job displacement, is crucial. Society must proactively manage the integration of robots into various sectors to ensure a harmonious coexistence, safeguarding both efficiency and human welfare.

There are conflicting opinions regarding whether competitive sports are beneficial to teenagers. This essay will analyze arguments on both sides before deducting my personal opinion.

On the one hand, competitive sports allow youths to experience their growing in skills step by step, therefore encourage them to become practical and perseverant. To be more specific, in order to win in sports competition, teenagers need to keep practicing their skills and learn lessons from every practice. For example, a badminton player would need to receive a training of non-stop running for 10 kilometers as well as practicing the same technical move over hundreds of times on a daily basis, in an attempt to develop their skills of the badminton gradually. Such arduous processes will teach teenagers that growing and success are the results from perseverance and hard working. Therefore, they will have a stronger heart and be able to constantly apply themselves when having a clear target in their future life.

Question: In some countries, more and more people are becoming interested in finding out about the history of the house or building they live in.
What are the reasons for this? 
How can people research this?

The history of a house or a building can be fascinating, sometimes daunting or even mesmerising at times if we try to delve into it. For some people, learning about the history of the houses, in which they live, is utterly important for various reasons. This essay attempts to outline some of those possible reasons for this and a couple of methods to research this.

The first possible reason for many to become inquisitive about the past of their houses could be that they actually want to find a connection, if any, between themselves and the buildings. After all, nobody would want to put their lives at risk by choosing to live in a “weak” building that was built with some “unreliable” materials about a century ago! 

But, for whatever reasons that they want to learn about the history of their buildings, it is always better that they ask the locals first to get their information about the former residents of their houses. They could also contact the local municipality or the concerned local authority who could apprise them about how the buildings were made. Finally, people could also visit a local library or the authority that keeps the information about old buildings, to learn about the history of buildings in their respective areas. 

To conclude, people are becoming more and more interested in the history of their houses primarily to find a unique feature of it to feel special or to learn about the architectural style and safety features of the house. They can contact local residents, municipality offices and the library to do the research work required to find the history of their houses.

Question: The best way to teach children to cooperate is through team sports at school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
In today’s modern society, some people think that the best approach for children to cooperate is team sports. I firmly believe that engaging in sports at school teaches children cooperation though it is among many options teachers can choose.

On the one hand, there are many reasons that team sports are one of the ways to help children develop team skills. First, team sports demand students to work closely and communicate effectively. This is mainly because children may be more interested in improving their communication skills and contact with others when they take part in an activity of team sports. Thus, during the process, children can learn to be a team player. Second, team sports help children learn valuable life lessons such as the role/importance of working together. For instance, when playing football, students will learn that they can only achieve success when they cooperate with each other effectively. This may help develop their teamwork spirit in the future.

On the other hand, I am firmly convinced that apart from team sports at school, other methods can also develop children’s corporate skills. To begin with, teachers can divide students into groups in class to study. This means that children can work with others through a team in all subjects such as math, literature and physics. Thus, students may improve their teamwork skills and help each other to finish tasks such as presentations or essays. In addition, another way for children to practice cooperation outside their school is to play video games in moderation. The main reason for this is that there are a lot of games that require players to work together efficiently in order to win. For example, in the game League of Legends, players have to compete against each other in teams of five members.

In conclusion, although team sports at school can teach children to cooperate, I personally think that there are better measures such as promoting group work in class and playing games moderately that can be adopted to encourage their students to work in a team.

Question: It is important for all towns and cities to have large public spaces such as squares
and parks. Do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
Many people claim that large public spaces are an indispensable part in every city’s infrastructure. While it is true that those spaces significantly improve residents’ living standard, I would argue that they are not suitable for all cities in the world.
To begin with, there are several advantages of communal places that cannot be neglected. Firstly, squares and parks provide citizens with free enormous spaces and beautiful green areas, which are ideal for people to keep exercising. Therefore, outdoor public locations are important to residents’ physical health. Since individuals are fit and healthy, they work more effectively and contribute more to society. Secondly, due to the development of modern technology, many people are spending very little time  interacting with society. Therefore, having easy access to outdoor communal room helps people get involved in different social activities and strengthen the human bonding. For example, at the weekend a teenager can go to the park with his or her friends for camping or chatting instead of staying at home and playing video games all day. 
However, I would argue that outdoor shared locations such as parks and squares are not suitable for all cities in the world. The first reason is that a number of cities such as Sao Paulo, Brazil and Mumbai, India are facing the problem of overpopulation. Therefore, those cities’ space should be utilized to build accommodation for citizens there instead of constructing big public areas. Another reason is that many undeveloped cities’ budgets are limited. Consequently, the expenditures on radical sectors such as education and medicine should be those cities’ priorities. Building such enormous shared places will be an unnecessary burden on cities’ financial budgets and lead to the decrease of government spending on other important sectors
In sum, there is no doubt that outdoor public spaces are beneficial to citizens’ quality of lives. However, I believe that building those constructions or not is up to each city’s condition and financial budget.

Question: In cities and towns all over the world the high volume of traffic is a problem. 


What are the causes of this and what actions can be taken to solve this problem?

Essay:
Traffic congestion is a serious issue in many parts of the world. This is because of the poor infrastructure of the roads and lack of proper public transports .Improving the public transport systems and proper connectivity of roads will solve the issue to some extent.

One  main reason for high traffic jams is that roads are not properly connected and narrow lanes of the main roads of the cities.Most of the working-class people, as well as school children, start their day at the same time.If there are no flyovers,underground bridges or additional lanes,traffic gets concentrated at the same place.Moreover,insufficient lanes for many vehicles to pass through at the same time increase the problem.Furthermore,many cities have not improved public transport systems forcing people to take personal vehicles.For instance,even if each member of a family takes their vehicle for work then traffic problems aggravate.These are the reasons for a high volume of traffic jams in the developed part of the world.

The main solution for overcoming this issue is to increase connectivity  in roads.Constructing fly-over bridges,underground passages will help in diverting traffic to a certain level.Additional by-lanes connecting the main road also divert traffic present on the main roads.Another solution is upgrading public transport systems at regular intervals in the urban areas.Government should increase local buses in the routes where traffic jam is seen the most.Also,new forms of transport like over-head metro rails do make a big difference in reducing the volume.For example,Dubai,one of the busiest cities in the world constructed Dubai metro rail as an answer to their traffic woes.These solutions help in overcoming traffic jam issues to a large extent.

To conclude,high vehicular traffic congestion is a major issue in the modern world.Bad infrastructure and poor connectivity are the cause of this problem;however,improving connectedness and increasing public transport services solve this problem to a large extent.

Question: The typical teaching situation of a teacher and students in the class will not exist by the year 2050. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
It is believed that the learning model in which students and teachers must go to school to access knowledge will be replaced by the year 2050. Although there are several reasons for this forecast, I believe that this kind of teaching model plays an indispensable role in students’ acquisition of knowledge.

On the one hand, advocates of this idea may have some rationales to argue that the year 2050 will not record the presence of the existing learning model. Firstly, the introduction of online learning platforms has enabled learners to access information regardless of physical barriers. For example, students in different countries can have access to a variety of knowledge from physics to arts with the clicks of the mouse, which facilitates learners from long distances. Moreover, recently, artificial intelligence (AI) has been introduced in educational sectors, which assesses students’ learning process and then dispenses personalized instructions as well as feedback with astonishing accuracy rates. All of which used to be the functionality of teachers and therefore, the physical presence of educators has been questioned. 

However, although technology innovation offers learners a wide variety of knowledge, students may not comprehensively understand it. For example, whether an unemotional and rigid teaching machine can convey knowledge as efficiently as teachers whose teaching approach is varied to suit different types of students. They can be amiable and helpful to students who struggle with acquiring knowledge or strict to learners who slack off their studies. Furthermore, the learning process is not only the acquisition of theoretical knowledge but also practical skills. A classroom that includes the physical presence of students and teachers plays a role as a small-scale society and therefore students in the class have the opportunity to be exposed to different counterparts with different characteristics, therefore, improving their interpersonal skills and team-working skills. 

In conclusion, although the role of teachers and existing learning models are under threat due to technological innovation, I believe they can not be replaced because they bring about many benefits for students’s academic performance and practical skills.

Over the past decades, environmental problems have never failed to draw public attention  and provoke debates. Firstly, it is important to recognize that although the occurrence of positive outcome towards environment is almost inevitable, the final result may not be as expected for long. Some may  hold optimistic attitude that this particular approach would be the effect on limiting the  number of cars and thereby reducing the amount of environment-damaging gas emission. This  argument could be true to some extent. However, they should take into account the fact that  since the cost of public transport would also be affected, resistance in people with the need of  travel seems to be inevitable, hence the impossibility of achieving the desired goal. Therefore,  increasing fuel prices will not make any significant changes.  Secondly, it is equally important to recognize that there is evidence that waste gas from cars is  not the leading cause of air pollution. The opponents may argue that the combustion of fossil  fuels by cars is the main producer of carbon dioxide. Nevertheless, they are ignorant of the fact  that the chef culprit is the discharge of pollutants into the atmosphere due to the rapidly growing  manufacturing industry. Governments could better handle this problem if they could increase  control over industrial waste-discharge and adopt more environmental friendly materials and  production equipment. For example, wind and tidal power in the Netherlands, nuclear power in  Japan and solar power in the United States have all proven their efficiency  in energy  production. This example indicates that other solutions could be employed in other parts of the  world to minimize the global dependence on fossil fuel.  In conclusion, under no circumstances should increasing the price of fuels be taken as the best  solution to environmental issues, as it has neglected both the reaction of consumers and the  root cause of the problem as mentioned above.

It is a well-known fact that the children better learn through images than text, therefore teachers use various art pieces to explain them many historical events. According to a survey, it was found that children who learned the story through snapshots were able to retain that information for longer duration as compared to others. Additionally, children learn to express themselves via creativity. Art helps children in communicating many concepts which they otherwise find difficult to explain.

On the other hand, many people believe that art is not an important subject to be taught at school because it does not add any value to their profile as other subjects such as math and science does. Simple mathematics calculations are always used in later stages of life, so it is important to learn the math at school level, but this is not the case with Art. Moreover, art does not help children in finding a job when they reach adulthood. This skill is not given much weightage by any employer.

In conclusion, art may not help children in getting a good job or may not be used in practical life when they reach adulthood, but in childhood it helps children immensely by encouraging them to learn about their culture.

Question: The only way to improve road safety is to give much stricter punishments on driving offenses. 

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
There is currently a debate about whether imposing stricter penalties on inappropriate drivers is the sole solution to promoting road safety. I strongly disagree with this statement because, in my view, road safety depends not only on the severity of punishments but also on effective traffic rule enforcement and heightened public awareness.

One compelling reason why I argue that traffic rules play a pivotal role in addressing this issue is that rules form the fundamental framework that shapes societal behavior. Moreover, stringent traffic laws can deter drivers from engaging in dangerous behaviors on the road, thereby fostering a safer driving environment. To illustrate, individuals contemplating driving home after consuming alcoholic beverages, which could lead to accidents, are more likely to reconsider their actions when faced with the consequences outlined in traffic laws. Consequently, rules are instrumental in preventing potentially hazardous situations.

Another key factor supporting my stance is the importance of individual awareness and responsibility in ensuring road safety. Despite the existence of stringent penalties in traffic laws, some individuals continue to flout them. By educating drivers about these laws and cultivating a mindset of respect for fellow citizens on the road, we can significantly improve driver behavior. For example, a well-informed driver with a positive attitude toward road safety is more likely to become a responsible and law-abiding motorist, thereby contributing to a safer traffic environment. Therefore, encouraging a collective commitment to safe driving is paramount in enhancing road safety.

In conclusion, I firmly believe that achieving road safety requires more than just imposing harsher penalties on offenders. It necessitates a multifaceted approach that includes effective traffic rule enforcement and the cultivation of public awareness and responsibility. By addressing these aspects comprehensively, we can work towards building a safer and more secure road environment for everyone.

Question: Some people believe that time spent on television, video and computer games can be valuable for children. Others believe this has negative effects on a child. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

Essay:
Interactive media such as television, video, and computer games has been used by children in their free time frequently. However, while some people think that it is important to use these devices for kids for educational purpose and stress-release, I personally believe that mentioned stuff contain bad influence for them.

With regard to the educational purpose, people believe it is acceptable for several reasons. Firstly, they think that interactive media can be a source of learning to these children. This is because media can offer audio and visual-based learning that allows children to absorb knowledge in fun way. That being said, parents may feel less worry if their children play gadgets, as long as the content accessed is education-related material. Furthermore, it is believed by some research that learning by video is easily stuck in our memory rather than textbook-based learning. 

However, I do not argue these arguments are entirely valid. To begin, it has been shown on numerous occasion that children who spent leisure times more than four hours to videos are subject to lack of emotional control. This has caused many children are quickly agitated if their devices are taken away. If the goal is to ensure children to study interactively, then these emotional problem should not happen in the first place at all. Therefore, again, leaving children with devices should not be considered as alternative to interactive learning.

To sum up, although some people argue that interactive media provides positive effects for children for studying purpose, I would argue there is sufficient evidence to demonstrate that this is not the case, and therefore, controlling the usage of medias for children should be under strict supervision.

Question: Children find it difficult to concentrate on or pay attention to school. 
What are the reasons? How can we solve this problem?

Essay:
Education plays a pivotal role in children’s developmental years, and the quality of which requires the dedication of both students and teachers. Unfortunately, it is found that children in schools are not engrossed in study. Does this mean that teachers are unqualified or are students themselves to blame? What are the remedies to overcome this problem?
Adolescents’ innate characteristics should be brought into close scrutiny. Children, as non-grownups, are generally less self-disciplined. This means that they are ofttimes unable to control their concentration, easily affected by distractions such as a sudden sound or an idea that pops up and is unrelated with the class.  Each time students get sidetracked, they would miss the important points that teachers are elaborating. To combat this productivity-damaging weakness, there should be more research on strengthening children’s concentration. The ability to focus on important tasks for a longer duration of time could keep students from absent-mindedness and boost learning efficiency.
Another cause of this problem is attributed to ineffective teaching. These days, many teachers are not doing a good job. They constantly adopt teacher-centred methods in class, without taking into account students’ preferences.  This inappropriate method could demotivate students, making them lose interest in study. The solution would be to opt for a student-centred attitude. Teachers could integrate into their class livelier and more inspiring elements, so that the classes they teach would be more in line with young people’s taste.  With an intense interest in what the teachers are saying, the students would voluntarily engross themselves in these absorbing topics.
In summary, adolescents’ shortcoming in self-discipline and the mechanical teaching strategy chosen by teachers are held accountable for pupils’ inability to focus on study. The suggested recipes are to enhance those young people’s concentration and to put a higher value on what they are fond of.

Question: Some people think that museums should be enjoyable places to entertain people, while others believe that the purpose of museums is to educate.
Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

Essay:
Recently, people have had contrasting views on the purpose of museums. While some individuals argue that its role is to entertain visitors, others believe that it should be an educational role. In this essay, both sides of the argument will be discussed in detail and I will provide my opinion why I support the former view. 

On the one hand, it can be argued that the main purpose of museums is entertainment. Since they are tourist-attraction places, they should exhibit enjoyable objects and programmes. In other words, if tourists have to read too much educational content, they may quickly get bored. Therefore, some museums have interactive activities or even games to encourage people to visit them. The most salient example of this is the Chocolate Museum in Korea and the Cheese Museum in the Netherlands. Thus, museums may be considered mainly as recreational places. 

On the other hand, some people might argue that museums should have an educational role. This is because they showcase the country’s valuable cultural items. For instance, The Egyptian Museum in Cairo which exhibits plenty of pharaonic objects. Therefore, some museums employ a tour guide in order to explain the history of every piece to tourists. Other places offer CDs or brochures for the same purpose. Indeed, only when visitors are taught this information will it be possible to save such a culture.

In conclusion, although some individuals believe that museums’ fundamental role is to entertain its visitors, I think the purpose of them should be educational in order to save the culture as well as the history of the country.

Question: Some people believe that the government should not spend money on international aid when they have their own disadvantaged people like homeless and unemployed. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
Over the last 100 years, population has grown at an exponential rate across many countries in the world. This brings along with it its own problems such as poverty, illiteracy, unemployment and so on. Many governments allocate huge resources to tackle these problems. Since all governments have problems to solve in their own countries, I agree with the argument that their first priority should be their own people.

There are ample reasons why I believe that the government should put the welfare of its own people ahead of others. To begin with, financial resources are becoming scarce and many countries are already in debt. These funds must be reserved for the development and maintenance of its own institutions and social security measures such as free health care and shelters for homeless people. Secondly, such welfare schemes not only elevate people out of poverty; they also help the government indirectly by creating jobs. This, in turn, facilitates the economic growth of the country.

On the other hand, it is understandable and reasonable to donate money to the poorer nations as a gesture of basic human decency and humanity. No nation, after all, can live in prosperity when its neighbours are struggling with poverty. By offering financial assistance to their poor neighbours, countries can also put a curb on illegal immigration. Even so, in my opinion, solving problems in one’s own country is more important than venturing to help others. Others should be helped only when the donating country has a surplus of money and resources.

In conclusion, there are obvious benefits for the government in the long run from donating money as relief aids to many foreign countries. However, I strongly iterate that the government must first improve the economic, financial and employment prospects of its own people before embarking on humanitarian work abroad.

Question: Some people think that art is an essential subject for children at school while others think it is a waste of time. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

Essay:
In this day and age, children are required to study a great deal of subjects at school. Although some believe that studying art is a waste of time for children at institutions, others support that it is mandatory for them to learn art. In this essay, I will examine both views and explain why I think it is necessary to include art education at school.

There are two main reasons why a number of people think it was a waste of time. Firstly, students should spend their time on practical subjects such as sciences and languages. By doing so, they can sharpen their skills for  future workplaces. Secondly, artworks are too complicated for children to understand. Most of the students find it difficult to interpret the symbolism of the post-impressionism paintings. Owing to a lack of life experience, they usually fail to integrate their viewpoints into the masterpieces. If they find it boring, it will only cost their invaluable time for nothing.

Whereas it shows that learning art is hard and seems useless for kids, there are precise values that they can obtain through studying art. The most prominent one is understanding history. Thanks to collectors who preserved thousands of art pieces, students not only can experience what living in the Middle Ages looked like by looking at  oil paintings, but also learn from others’ experiences and interpretations of wars, disasters, and historical events. Moreover, they can also improve self-awareness by knowing their own preferences. The more artwork they learn, the better self they will understand.

Art is an abstract subject that people hold different views on whether it should be a mandatory subject for children to study. By carefully assessing both views, I wholeheartedly believe that art is an invaluable subject for students at school.

Question: Increases in the production of consumer goods results in damage to the natural environment.  Why is this the case?  What can be done to solve this problem?

There is a widespread saying that an ever-increasing pace of consumer goods manufactured will lead to more adverse effects on our natural world. There are several reasons obviously cause this severe problem, and solutions could certainly be taken to tackle it immediately. 
This alarming problem could be contributed by some following factors. First and foremost, the increase in the production of consumer products would trigger the natural resource depletion. Specifically, the more people produce consumer goods, the more naturals resources are used during the manufacturing process, leading to the ecological imbalance. Deforestation is an evident example to satisfy the high demand of space for factories and plants, which can cause host of serious problem for human beings like climate change and desertification. Another important factor is that more industrial waste is discharged directly from manufacturing factories into the environment. Consequently, this can lead to global warming, which may have a devasting affect on the planet in the future.
In term of solutions, it is believed that both individuals and governments should join hand to mitigate the problem. At the level of individuals, each person should attempt to reduce their unnecessary consumption and change their throw-away behavior. As a result, the decline in the demand of consumer products will be the premise of slowing down the environmental degradation. Besides, national authorities should implement policies which force manufacturing factories to adopt waste treatment system and energy-saving equipment. Such these effective systems would clean industrial sewage before dumping it into the environment, or even recycle the waste for the next production. 
In conclusion, our planet is severely impacted by the increase in the production of consumer goods. To address this issue, individuals and governments could certainly put effort to change the consumption behavior as well as force the companies take responsible for the impact they have on the environment.

Question: As transport and accommodation problems are increasing in many cities, some governments are encouraging businesses to move to rural areas. Do you think the advantage outweigh the disadvantage?

Essay:
Some governments are recommending companies to relocate to the countryside to address the transport and housing problems in cities. This strategy is believed to have both benefits and drawbacks. In this essay, both sides will be explored, followed by my opinion.

On the one hand, one advantage of this strategy is the potential for economic growth and job creation in rural areas. By attracting more companies to the countryside, this area can experience an influx of investment, leading to increased business and manufacturing activities in this region which can create more employment opportunities for local residents. This can help revatilize local economies, reduce the unemployment rate and improve the overall standard of living in this area. In addition, this trend can alleviate the issues related to transport and housing in crowded cities. By decentralizing business activities, this strain on urban infrastructure can be reduced, leading to improved transport flow and less pressure on housing and public services. In other words, this approach can create a more sustainable and livable environment in metropolis. 

On the other hand, there are also drawbacks that need to be considered. One major challenge is the availability of skilled workers in the countryside. To be more specific, companies may have difficulties in finding a qualified workplace, especially in specialized industries that require advanced education and specific expertise. This circumstance not only pose a barrier to attracting companies to rural regions but also hinders their potential growth. Moreover, the countryside may lack neccessary infrastructure and amenities that support businesses, such as a reliable transport network, access to the market and adequate ultilities. These limitations have a profound impact on their competitiveness and viability. Another consideration is the potential influence on social fabric of local communities. In fact, this approach may lead to changes in local cultures, traditions and ways of life. Thus, it is essential that the development is sustainable and respects the value and needs of local people.

In conclusion, although encouraging companies to move to rural areas can bring economic benefits in this regions and address some issues in cities, this stratey also has some disadvantages that should be considered carefully. By striking a balance between economic growth, social consideration and environmental sustainability, governments can promote a balanced regional prosperity and create opportunities for both rural and urban regions.

Question: The best way to teach children to cooperate is through team sports at school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
The idea that team sports at school are the best way to teach children to cooperate is widely supported. I strongly agree with this view, as team sports, such as basketball and futsal, require players to collaborate and suppress their egos.

Through team sports, students learn how to play for their team and improve their ability to understand other players. To win, players must cooperate with one another, and this is not possible if they do not trust each other. For example, in basketball, each player has a unique position and responsibility, and they must support each other to score. They cannot play for themselves if they want to beat their opponents. This approach teaches children to collaborate and work with others, skills that they can apply in other settings, such as schoolwork, work, and building their own business.

Additionally, team sports help to reduce children's tendency to focus solely on themselves, a characteristic that is common among young people. In team sports, they must abandon the idea of being the best and focus on the team's goal. For example, if the target is to win a futsal tournament, they must stick to their strategy, which every member of the team must follow. This approach fosters unity and helps children learn to cooperate effectively.

In conclusion, participating in sports that require more than one person to play is an effective way to build children's collaboration skills. They learn unconsciously how to work as part of a team and how to use their skills to support their teammates. Furthermore, playing team sports makes children happier because of the production of dopamine during the game, making them more receptive to learning cooperation skills.

Question: Whether or not someone achieve their aims is mostly by a question of luck. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
Many people claim that luck is the most crucial element contributing to a person's success. While I accept that luck does have an important role in helping people reach their targets, I would argue that hard work and determination are much more crucial factors leading to the achievement of an individual. 

On the one hand, I agree that luck can be an important factor. First, some people are fortunate enough to be born in a wealthy family, which allows them to have a better education or to easily start their own business without having to borrow money from someone else. As a result, these people tend to have better opportunities to succeed than those coming from poor families. Furthermore, some individuals are lucky to be given great talents which others do not have. For example, Mozart was able to play music when he was very young, or Lionel Messi already had great football skills when he was born. 

However, I would argue that although luck can be necessary, it is not the most crucial factor leading to success. Firstly, people need to work really hard and put much effort into their jobs if they want to be successful. For instance, before becoming one of the best football players in the world, Cristiano Ronaldo had to go through intense training hours every day for many years. Secondly, a person is less likely to reach his targets if he does not have determination. On the way leading to success, there might be many difficulties, and people need to keep moving forward to overcome those challenges. 

In conclusion, while I agree that luck is important to some extent in helping people become successful, I believe that hard work and determination are the most important elements.

Question: Many people feel that all teenagers should have to do unpaid work during their free time to help the local community and for the benefit of society as a whole. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
There is a new idea circulating among some experts which states that teenagers should do charity work on their holidays in order to gain a deeper appreciation and help their local communities. Although I believe that there are some merits to such arguments, I have to disagree with such notions and in this ,essay I will try to reason my perspective and draw a conclusion.

On the one hand, it is foolish to assume that teenagers are not able to help their societies. The bright mind of such young humans can instantly learn and practice new talents in new circumstances. For instance, I experienced this first-hand when a teenager learned how to analyze some experimental data almost overnight and was able to help us reach our conference deadline. Therefore, these individuals are capable of helping their communities in meaningful ways.

However, I think that teenagers should be reimbursed for such jobs. First, I believe that if they are not paid sufficiently, they are going to lose their motive and will not do the task up to standards. For example, a teenager might feel that the task is imposed upon him/her and as a result do not perform satisfactorily. Thus, it is of utmost importance to motivate such individuals, and money can do this very well. Second, I think that such notions might harm these young humans by avoiding  

the opportunity of studying in their free time or learning essential skills that might prove useful in the future. For one, I  learned basic programming in my free time when I was a teenager. So, I believe that it will be cruel to force teenagers to do such things without any kind of pay.

To sum up, it is indeed obvious that younger generations can be useful for their societies, however, if one has to work one must be reimbursed for it so as to raise their motivation. Additionally, any form of work should not devoid them of their valued time. Nevertheless, as far as I am concerned, governments should legislate rules in order to use this young workforce and pay them in preparing their attitude and behaviour.

In conclusion, the massive amount of vehicles on the roads has many causes such as poor transportation as well as lacking  facilities. Question: Some people think that one of the best ways to solve environment problems is to increase the cost of fuel for cars and vehicles (agree/disagree).

Essay:
As environmental issues have plagued our society for years, people have proposed several solutions to help mitigate them. One suggested way is concerned with raising the fuel costs for various vehicles. However, I tend to disagree with this proposal. 

Some may argue that with the increment in gasoline, the number of automobiles would be effectively limited, and thus air problems in cities could be addressed. When car owners feel reluctant to drive in the face of high driving expenditures, they are encouraged to choose greener way of travelling, such as walking or bicycling. In this way, exhaust fumes released from engine combustion are very likely to decline, resulting in cleaner atmosphere for urban areas. Nevertheless, this perspective fails to take into account this: price is not the only reason for citizens to select certain traffic mode. For those who live in suburbs and work in downtown, for example, they have to drive to commute, and therefore, may still cling to the original travelling method, despite the increase in fuel expenses. 

To lift the petrol expenditure to curb environmental issues can have devastating repercussions. First, private drivers have heavier financial burdens, which could bring more pressure on their work and family life. Moreover, the rise in fuels can also harm other productive activities. Take agriculture as an example: if farmers have to spend more on operating agricultural vehilcles (for instance, ploughs, tractors), they will face a higher production costs and a diminish in profits, and in a long run, this could mean price swings in the crop market. 

To conclude, making it more expensive to drive seems to be a cure for air pollution, but this is not effective enough and can bring undesirable consequences. The government needs to devise meticulous plans for addressing green issues.

If all children were sent to free schools, they would be taught a more modern mindset, which celebrates liberation and personal growth, becoming independent individuals who can find their own way out of impoverishment.

Nevertheless, I acknowledge the importance of other approaches in an effort to support impoverished people. For instance, financial organisations should provide funding for upgrading infrastructure with better-connected roads and bridges. These would not only foster economic growth but also cultural exchanges that enable sustainable development.

In conclusion, I mostly agree with the idea of offering 6 years of schooling free of charge with a view to ending poverty in developing nations as it makes it possible for young people to acquire basic knowledge and have a more liberal mindset even though additional initiatives such as infrastructure improvement should also be in place. That is why governments should develop a comprehensive plan to address the issue of poverty systematically.

In the modern society, artificial intelligent has changed our lives in many different ways. It is true that robots replace human workforce because of their accuracy and speed. Robots could do the same job much faster without errors than human. Moreover, thanks to the advent of artificial intelligent technology, people no longer to work in the dangerous situations. On the other hand, certain industries which require emotional connections such as lawyers, psychologists and nannies could not be substituted by robots. Even though robots have immense knowledge through their database, they could not fully interact with human. For instance, patients who suffer from mental illness could get some advice from robots, but they could not fully cure their mind as they do not feel they were treated as human. Therefore, they cannot replace some of jobs which need for human interactions.

In conclusion, robots are already taken some jobs from human but not all the jobs could be replaced by artificial intelligent robots as we still need interpersonal skills for certain industries.

Question: In many places women are taking jobs which are traditionally done by men. What do you think make these changes happen? What is your opinion about it?

Essay:
In contemporary settings, due to the prevalence of the feminist movement, more and more females are hired in some industries which conventionally are the domains of males. The contributors of this transformation will be discussed in this essay along with the reasons why I believe this is a blessing rather than a curse. Multiple factors facilitate this trend.

 To be more specific, an increasing number of women receive tertiary education and thus, the professional knowledge obtained from such experience enables them to enter / join some companies, working as engineers, scientists and lawyers. In addition, several decades ago, most tasks were performed by hand, which made men in an advantageous position due to their relatively stronger bodies. By contrast, nowadays, the vast majority of manual jobs are performed by machines, and the requirement for workers is not strength but the skills of operating these mechanics, which makes the females on a par with their male counterparts. 

This improvement exerts a positive influence on both females and their families. Women are always detail-oriented, so if they are working as scientists or doctors, they have higher chances of obtaining huge success. A good example is a female scientist Madame Curie who attributed her success in the discovery of the element Ra to the fact that she identified the minor difference in their daily research outcomes. Consequently, by focusing on these divergences and doing deep research, she found the element and reaped a breakthrough in their research. Besides, formerly, the roles of women were confined to being housewives, which earned them no salaries. Hence, their families depended on their husbands’ salaries, but in  modern times, the combined salaries of both husbands and wives enable them to have better lifestyles.

In conclusion, the reasons for the increase in women’s involvement in work which used to be done by men are their educational qualifications and the development of technologies which eliminate manual labour.

Question: More and more people are becoming seriously overweight. Some people think a solution can be to increase the price of fattening foods. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
In this day and age, gaining weight is a global problem. The increasing number of residents are becoming victims of obesity. Some people argue that to solve this situation, it is necessary to go up the expenditure of food which is high in fat. It seems to me that, being overweight is not only by food but also due to human habits. I will shed light on my opinion in the following essay.

On the one hand, there is no denying that pricing fattening foods at a higher cost can demonstrate some effectiveness in reducing the risk of obesity. Firstly, when unhealthy food items become more expensive, people are more likely to reconsider their choices and seek out more nutritious options. For instance, if a bottle of sugary water costs more than a bottle of water, people will choose the latter, thereby reducing their calorie intake. Secondly, this price growth will motivate individuals to reduce the frequency and quantity of purchases, reducing overall consumption and thereby the likelihood of obesity.

On the other hand, other measures with far-reaching impacts should be given greater consideration. Nowadays, a large number of people are leading a sedentary lifestyle which is considered as one of the major reasons for obesity. Therefore, physical exercise plays a vital role in maintaining a healthy body. Besides, participating in counseling sessions with nutrition experts can provide valuable insights into a healthy and balanced diet. For example, by gradually transitioning from fat-heavy to more nourishing food options, individuals can make better-informed choices for their daily diet, leading to a significant decrease in obesity rates over the long run.

In conclusion, it can be argued that while the rise in fattening food prices can be a viable solution to a certain extent, other measures still need to be taken to comprehensively reduce this obesity circumstance

The essay adequately addresses the given task by discussing the extent to which increasing the price of fattening foods can be an effective solution to the problem of overweight individuals. However, the drawbacks can not be underestimated. The main problem caused by giving birth later is related to the fertility of both genders. Question: The best way to solve the world’s environmental problems is to increase the cost of fuel for cars and other vehicles. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Essay:
The world we are living in is, unfortunately, facing loads of serious environmental problems. There is an idea that says if we want to solve these problems, the best way is to increase the cost of petrol. Although I agree that we must deal with environmental issues, I do not think the mentioned solution is a smart choice.

Firstly, the rise in fuel price is likely to be counter-intuitive because it would put a lot of burden on the economy. Everyone would be affected, from workers whose companies are far away from their homes, or parents who have to travel long distances to take their children to school, to a stressed person who just wants to go somewhere outside to relax. Businesses would have to pay much more for delivery, and some would even close down because of losses. If this happened for a long time, it would lead to an economic crisis.

Instead, I believe that a much better solution would be to boost researches into and manufacture of vehicles that use clean energy. Gasoline cost might go up, but that would not reduce people’s need for travelling. Therefore, we need to give them other options instead of forcing them to give up their only choice. Electric motorbikes and cars are the kinds of vehicles we can take into consideration. In fact, these have become very popular with people in my country, Vietnam, during recent years. This could be more successful when we can mass produce these means of transport and make them more affordable. 

In conclusion, I do not agree with the idea that raising fuel cost is the best solution to environmental problems because this will make matters worse by damaging the economy. Rather than that, we should focus on researching and producing vehicles using clean energy.

Question: Some people believe that eventually all jobs will be done by artificially intelligent robots. What is your opinion?

However, tasks that require emotional intelligence will continue to stay with human workforce. This essay will discuss why a few jobs will be done by artificially intelligent robots rather than all jobs.

All operational and repetitive tasks, which require less skills, will be done by robots in the coming years. Repetitive jobs can be easily automated because it follows a regular pattern. Moreover, these jobs require lesser human intervention for execution. For example, during the industrial revolution, machines were employed to carry out mundane tasks which were repetitive in nature. Similarly, automated teller machine is another example of a job which was replaced by a robot.

In contrast, jobs that need emotional touch can only be executed by humans. Robots work on logical programming, but emotional decisions are taken based on many situational inputs that cannot be programmed. Psychaitrist, for instance, is a career that needs to work closely with the patient to understand the emotional state of the patient. Even though the symptoms shown by patients with same mental disease might be similar, the treatments differ from patient to patient.

To sum up, eventually robots will be used to help us with all menial jobs; however sophisticated jobs that require human intervention will be done by humans. Ultimately, a few human jobs will be considered for robotic automation. Majority of the tasks done by humans will stay with humans.

Question: Consumers are faced with increasing numbers of advertisements from competing companies. To what extent do you think consumers are influenced by advertisements? What measures can be taken to protect them?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Essay:
Consumers are undoubtedly influenced by the vast number of advertisements bombarding them daily. The extent of this influence varies, but it's undeniable that advertising plays a significant role in shaping consumer behavior. Various measures can be implemented to protect consumers from potentially misleading or harmful effects of advertisements.

Influence of Advertisements, firstly,  Psychological Impact;  Advertisements often leverage psychological tactics to create emotional connections with consumers, influencing their preferences and purchase decisions. For example, emotionally compelling advertisements can shape perceptions and build brand loyalty. Secondly, Brand Recognition; Repetition and exposure through advertising contribute to brand recognition. Consumers are more likely to choose familiar brands, even if they are not necessarily the best or most suitable for their needs. Third, Social Influence, Social media advertisements and influencer marketing can significantly impact consumer choices. Recommendations from peers and influencers can create a sense of trust and credibility, influencing purchasing decisions.

Measures to Protect Consumers; fundamentaly, transparency in Advertising; Governments and regulatory bodies should enforce transparency in advertising practices. Companies must provide accurate information about their products or services, preventing misleading claims or false representations. Sequentially, Educating Consumers; Promoting media literacy and consumer education is crucial. By enhancing consumers' critical thinking skills, they can better discern between honest advertisements and those employing manipulative tactics. Another way , Stricter Regulations; Governments can introduce and enforce stricter regulations on advertising content. This includes monitoring and penalizing companies that engage in deceptive advertising or make false claims about their products. Moreover, Ethical Standards for Influencers; Establishing ethical standards for influencers in the digital space is essential. Clear guidelines and regulations can prevent the endorsement of products based solely on financial incentives without genuine belief in their quality. For example,

In the pharmaceutical industry, governments rigorously regulate drug advertisements to ensure that the information presented is accurate and not misleading. Strict guidelines mandate the inclusion of potential side effects, helping consumers make informed decisions about their health.

In Conclusion, Consumers are undoubtedly influenced by advertisements, and while this influence can be positive, it also raises concerns about deceptive practices. Implementing measures such as transparency, education, stricter regulations, and ethical standards can help protect consumers from potentially harmful effects and ensure a fair marketplace. A well-informed consumer base is key to fostering a marketplace where advertisements serve as informative tools rather than manipulative influences.

Question: Some people think competitive sport is important for a child’s education . Other think it has negative effects on children. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

Essay:
A few people believe that playing competitive games by students plays a vital role in their studies, whereas others assert involvement in these activities is not beneficial for the children. I intend to discuss both the views followed by my own opinion.

On the one hand, advocates of latter view opine that competitive sport can adversely impact the studies of the pupils. In order to participate at a level which requires consistent practice, students need to spend enough time in the field to participate in it. Due to this, they often fail to spend time in their academics, thereby negatively affecting their studies. For example, a child who practices in the morning and evening for sports gets tired and generally skips the classes and self-study hours to recover. This situation clearly depicts the effect on the education of  sports students as they do not get time for studies.

On the other hand, proponents of the former notion assert participation in competitive sport enhances certain skills which can assist the young ones to imitate these characters in their academic life. To explain, players are not only trained to bear pressure, but also to hold their nerves in any competition by the sports coaches. These qualities are generally required in taking competitive examinations as well, which are not easily provided through teaching in classes. Thus, students who are equipped with these skills through competitive sports activities are more likely to get succeeded in the examinations which require competition such as entrance exam for various prestigious universities and so on.

In my perspective, sports activities can aid the students to perform better in their education unless they spend a large share of time in the sports field only. It is primarily due to the fact that outdoor activities increase oxygen content in the body, which can make students more sharp and active. This is imperative for their studies because it can help them to raise their concentration while learning as the fresh and active mind is more focussed according to various studies as well.

To conclude, in my opinion, students ought to dedicate some time to competitive sports as it can help in terms of building character which can assist them in their education as well as refreshing their minds to increase concentration in studies.
